evidence_type: direct assay (synthetic/recombinant peptide; in vitro + mouse infection)
claim_tested: C5orf46 product kills Gram-negative bacteria, and is a cationic AMP
key_finding: Activity vs E. coli DH5a, E. coli O157:H7, V. cholerae, P. aeruginosa; efficacy in mouse O157:H7 model; cytotoxic to Jurkat and Raji. Authors describe AP-64 as 'an anionic amphiphilic peptide lacking cysteines (MW = 7.2, PI = 4.54)'. No membrane-permeabilization assay reported.
context: Human AP-64 (64 aa); four Gram-negative species; mouse; human lymphoma lines
confidence: High for the antibacterial activity claim. The killing MECHANISM is untested. Sole primary source for the activity.

citation: This analysis: UniProt Q6UWT4 + 1,451 KW-0929 mature peptides
key_finding: Net charge -6.10 at pH 7.4; pI 4.24; charge density -0.095 e/res. 1.5th percentile of 1,451 annotated mature AMPs (median +2.85); z = -2.50. D+E=16 vs K+R=10; 0 Cys.
context: Sequence level; UniProt CHAIN 24-87 = 64 aa = AP-64 exactly
confidence: High. Independently corroborated by the published pI 4.54. Limitation: descriptor prediction, not an assay.

claim_tested: The amphipathic helix presents a CATIONIC membrane-binding face
key_finding: Polar-face charge: AP-64 -1.0; LL-37 +6.0; magainin-2 +4.1; cecropin-A +2.0; DCD-1L 0.0.
confidence: High as a descriptor. Assumes canonical alpha-helical geometry.

claim_tested: Cationic character is the conserved, selected property of this family
key_finding: 21/21 mammalian mature regions net negative (-3.10 to -9.13); D+E > K+R in every one; 17/21 have zero Cys.
context: Primates, rodents, carnivores, ungulates, cetaceans, bats
confidence: High. Limitation: mature boundaries approximated by trimming 23 residues.

citation: This analysis: isoform + protease-site robustness test
claim_tested: A shorter cationic fragment could be the true effector
key_finding: No furin-like RX(K/R)R site. Best-case cuts after K19 or F22 give fragments of net -3.10 and -2.10. Isoform Q6UWT4-2 is a C-terminal truncation retaining the amphipathic window, mature net -4.14. No scenario yields net positive charge.
confidence: High. Closes the boundary-definition escape route.

citation: This analysis: Eisenberg moment + AlphaFold AF-Q6UWT4
key_finding: Max uH 0.602 at mature 30-47 (GTEIIENAVEFILRSMSR), 90.9th percentile; AlphaFold helix at precursor 45-68, pLDDT 75.3; acidic N-half pLDDT 54 (disordered, MobiDB-lite).
context: Sequence + AlphaFold2 monomer, no experimental structure
confidence: Moderate-high. pLDDT 75 is moderate; monomeric models miss membrane-induced folding.

claim_tested: Can AP-64 engage a lipid bilayer at all?
key_finding: Per-residue dG (unfolded): AP-64 full +0.467 (worst in set), acidic N-half +0.877, amphipathic window +0.328, LL-37 +0.347, cecropin-A +0.265. With the -0.40 helix term the AP-64 window (-0.072) matches LL-37 (-0.053) but full-length stays unfavourable (+0.067).
confidence: Moderate. Scale has no anionic-lipid term and applies to unfolded chains; helix bonus is an explicit assumption.

claim_tested: Which AMP class does the sequence actually resemble?
key_finding: Mahalanobis 3.56 (86th pct). All 15 nearest neighbours net-anionic (median -4.76): human chromogranin A fragments GR-44/ER-37/serpinin-RRG, bovine enkelytin and pancreastatin, 3 haptoglobin alpha chains, leech theromyzin, 2 Galleria anionic AMPs, VGF TLQP-62, snake LAAO fragments. Zero cationic lytic AMPs.
confidence: High as an unbiased class assignment. Limitation: descriptor similarity is not mechanistic proof.

claim_tested: AP-64 belongs to the proline-rich intracellular-target class
key_finding: AP-64 N-half 23.8% Pro, 0 Arg, 0 RP/PR dipeptides, 9 Asp. Bac7: 45.7% Pro, 11 Arg, 16 RP/PR, 0 Asp. PR-39: 48.7% Pro, 10 Arg, 11 RP/PR.
confidence: High; PrAMP uptake is Arg-dependent, AP-64 has 2 Arg in 64 residues.

claim_tested: How does an anionic human AMP engage membranes?
key_finding: DCD-1L at pH 7 (charge -2) has no effect on zwitterionic DOPC and permeabilizes DOPS only outside physiological transmembrane potential; Zn2+ restores permeabilization at physiological potential.
confidence: High for dermcidin. Extrapolation to AP-64 is inference, not evidence.

claim_tested: What defines the membrane-lytic class and its selectivity?
key_finding: Common features are net cationic charge from multiple Arg/Lys plus amphipathic structure; microbe-vs-host selectivity derives from anionic phospholipid content and host cholesterol.
context: Insect, horseshoe crab, frog, mammalian host-defence peptides
confidence: Review-level orientation. Explains why AP-64's anionic charge predicts the observed loss of selectivity.

claim_tested: Is cationic charge general to innate antibacterial effectors?
key_finding: 'Virtually all innate molecules that inactivate bacteria... are highly cationic in order to facilitate binding to the anionic bacterial cell envelopes.'
context: Defensins, cathelicidins, lysozyme, group IIA PLA2

claim_tested: Is cationic-LPS recognition required for Gram-negative OM permeabilization?
key_finding: Self-promoted uptake begins with electrostatic recognition of anionic LPS by cationic AMPs.

claim_tested: Does membrane-induced helicity alone predict membrane-disruptive killing?
key_finding: Four frog cathelicidin paralogs (+9 to -4) all formed membrane-induced helices, but only the +9 AS34 was membrane-disruptive; the anionic DL37 lacked direct antimicrobial effect.
confidence: High for the dissociation. Different family and organism.

claim_tested: Is C5orf46 expressed where a barrier AMP would act?
key_finding: Predicted secreted protein; RNA group-enriched: salivary gland 170.7, skin 112.2, blood vessel 85.7 nTPM; not detected in immune cells.
confidence: High for RNA. Gives opportunity for host defence; silent on mechanism.
